objective: Make breakage visible. Add one SNS alarm topic and CloudWatch alarms on every dead-letter queue, the HTTP API's 5xx count and p95/p99 latency, every Lambda function's errors and throttles, and RDS CPU, free storage and connections, each notifying the topic, so a failure no longer goes unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: Fanwire-Messaging contains exactly one AWS::SNS::Topic (the alarm topic), with a topic policy that denies publishing without TLS, and exports its ARN for the stacks that alarm into it. The template contains no AWS::SNS::Subscription: the address is set by hand, never committed.

Each dead-letter queue in Fanwire-Messaging (notification, ingestion-retry, media-scan-result) has an alarm on AWS/SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, Maximum over 5 minutes, GreaterThanThreshold 0, one evaluation period.
Fanwire-App has an alarm on the HTTP API $default stage's 5xx metric, Sum over 5 minutes, GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold 5.
Fanwire-App has two alarms on the HTTP API $default stage's Latency: p95 above 3000 ms and p99 above 8000 ms, each over 5-minute periods, 3 of 3 periods.

Every AWS::Lambda::Function in Fanwire-App has an Errors alarm (Sum over 5 minutes, GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold 1) and a Throttles alarm (Sum over 5 minutes, GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold 1), keyed on that function by FunctionName. A test derives the function list from the template, so a new function without alarms fails it.

There are alarms on the RDS instance: CPUUtilization Average above 80 percent for 3 of 3 5-minute periods; FreeStorageSpace Minimum below 2 GiB (2147483648 bytes); DatabaseConnections Maximum above 60.
Every alarm sends both its ALARM and its OK action to the alarm topic, and treats missing data as notBreaching.
A test counts the alarms across all synthesized stacks, so adding or removing one is a deliberate change to that test.
Fanwire-App outputs the alarm topic's ARN, so the human can subscribe an address to it.
infra/test/cfn-exec-policy.test.ts's TYPE_TO_IAM maps CloudWatch to cloudwatch and SNS to sns, and every cfn-exec-policy, iam-policy and permissions-boundary test passes in every domain mode.
